name: Brute Force Login Detection
description: Detects multiple failed authentication attempts from a single source IP within a time window.
spl:
index=windows EventCode=4625
| bucket _time span=5m
| stats count AS failed_attempts, values(Account_Name) AS accounts
    BY _time, Source_Network_Address
| where failed_attempts >= 10
| eval severity="HIGH", mitre_technique="T1110 - Brute Force"
| table _time, Source_Network_Address, failed_attempts, accounts, severity, mitre_technique
| sort -failed_attempts
tuning_notes: Adjust threshold (10) based on environment baseline. Whitelist service accounts if needed.
response: Block source IP at perimeter. Investigate whether any attempt succeeded (cross-reference EventCode=4624).

name: PowerShell Encoded Command Execution
description: Detects PowerShell invoked with -EncodedCommand or -Enc flags, commonly used to obfuscate malicious payloads.
spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 Image="*powershell.exe"
| where match(CommandLine, "-(?i)(enc|encodedcommand)\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}")
| eval decoded_hint=if(match(CommandLine,"IEX|Invoke-Expression"),"Likely download cradle","Unknown payload")
| stats count BY Computer, User, CommandLine, ParentImage, decoded_hint
| eval severity="CRITICAL", mitre_technique="T1059.001 - PowerShell Encoded Command"
| sort -count
| table Computer, User, ParentImage, CommandLine, decoded_hint, severity, mitre_technique
tuning_notes: Whitelist known admin scripts that legitimately use encoded commands. Validate base64 length threshold.
response: Isolate host immediately. Decode base64 payload. Check for download cradles or reflective loading.

name: Credential Dumping — LSASS Access
description: Detects access to lsass.exe process memory, indicative of credential dumping tools (Mimikatz, procdump).
spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=10 TargetImage="*lsass.exe"
| where GrantedAccess IN ("0x1010", "0x1410", "0x147a", "0x143a", "0x1fffff")
| stats count BY Computer, SourceImage, SourceUser, GrantedAccess, TargetImage
| eval risk=case(
    match(SourceImage,"mimikatz|procdump|wce|fgdump"),"CONFIRMED_TOOL",
    match(SourceImage,"taskmgr|msmpeng"),"LIKELY_BENIGN",
    true(),"SUSPICIOUS_UNKNOWN")
| where risk != "LIKELY_BENIGN"
| eval severity="CRITICAL", mitre_technique="T1003.001 - LSASS Memory"
| table Computer, SourceImage, SourceUser, GrantedAccess, risk, severity, mitre_technique
tuning_notes: Whitelist AV/EDR processes that legitimately access LSASS. Common FP sources: MsMpEng.exe, CrowdStrike.
response: Immediate host isolation. Run memory forensics. Assume all credentials on host are compromised — initiate password resets.

name: Lateral Movement via Pass-the-Hash
description: Detects network logons using NTLM with no associated interactive session — characteristic of pass-the-hash.
spl:
index=windows EventCode=4624
    Logon_Type=3 Authentication_Package=NTLM
| where NOT (Account_Name="ANONYMOUS LOGON" OR Account_Name="*$")
| stats count, values(Workstation_Name) AS src_hosts,
    dc(Workstation_Name) AS unique_src_hosts
    BY Account_Name, Source_Network_Address
| where unique_src_hosts >= 3 OR count >= 10
| eval severity="CRITICAL", mitre_technique="T1550.002 - Pass the Hash"
| sort -count
| table Account_Name, Source_Network_Address, count, unique_src_hosts, src_hosts, severity, mitre_technique
tuning_notes: Service accounts authenticating across many hosts will FP. Build a baseline of legitimate NTLM traffic first.
response: Identify originating host. Rotate Kerberos tickets (klist purge). Reset NTLM hashes. Consider enabling Credential Guard.

name: Persistence via Registry Run Keys
description: Detects new entries written to HKCU/HKLM Run registry keys — a common persistence mechanism.
spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=13
| where match(TargetObject,
    "CurrentVersion\\Run|CurrentVersion\\RunOnce|CurrentVersion\\RunServices")
| where NOT match(Image, "msiexec|setuphost|WindowsInstaller")
| stats count BY Computer, User, Image, TargetObject, Details
| eval persistence_type=case(
    match(TargetObject,"HKCU"),"User-Level Persistence",
    match(TargetObject,"HKLM"),"System-Level Persistence",
    true(),"Unknown")
| eval severity="HIGH", mitre_technique="T1547.001 - Registry Run Keys"
| table Computer, User, Image, TargetObject, Details, persistence_type, severity, mitre_technique
tuning_notes: Software installers frequently write Run keys. Build allowlist of known legitimate software.
response: Remove suspicious registry entry. Identify and kill associated process. Investigate parent process chain.

name: Suspicious Network Connections from Office Applications
description: Detects Office applications (Word, Excel) making outbound network connections — indicative of macro-based phishing.
spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=3
    Image IN ("*\\WINWORD.EXE","*\\EXCEL.EXE","*\\POWERPNT.EXE","*\\OUTLOOK.EXE")
| where NOT DestinationIp IN ("127.0.0.1","::1") AND Initiated=true
| where NOT match(DestinationHostname, "microsoft\.com|office\.com|live\.com|msn\.com")
| stats count, values(DestinationIp) AS dst_ips, values(DestinationPort) AS ports
    BY Computer, User, Image
| eval severity="HIGH", mitre_technique="T1566.001 - Spearphishing Attachment"
| sort -count
| table Computer, User, Image, dst_ips, ports, count, severity, mitre_technique
tuning_notes: Whitelist legitimate business domains. Some templates fetch from CDNs — validate against asset inventory.
response: Block outbound connection at firewall. Quarantine the document. Check if payload was downloaded.

name: Data Exfiltration via DNS Tunneling
description: Detects unusually high DNS query volume or oversized DNS responses — hallmarks of DNS tunneling (dnscat2, iodine).
spl:
index=network sourcetype=dns
| stats count AS query_count,
    avg(answer_length) AS avg_answer_len,
    dc(query) AS unique_queries,
    values(query_type) AS query_types
    BY src_ip, dest_ip
| where query_count > 500 OR avg_answer_len > 200 OR unique_queries > 300
| eval tunnel_indicator=case(
    avg_answer_len > 200, "HIGH: Large DNS responses",
    query_count > 500, "HIGH: Query volume spike",
    unique_queries > 300, "MEDIUM: High unique query entropy",
    true(), "NOMINAL")
| where tunnel_indicator != "NOMINAL"
| eval severity="HIGH", mitre_technique="T1071.004 - DNS Tunneling"
| table src_ip, dest_ip, query_count, unique_queries, avg_answer_len, tunnel_indicator, severity, mitre_technique
tuning_notes: CDN services and DNS resolvers will trigger volume alerts. Filter by internal src_ip ranges only.
response: Block DNS queries to suspicious resolver. Capture PCAP for payload analysis. Check for dnscat2/iodine signatures.

name: Ransomware — VSS Shadow Copy Deletion
description: Detects execution of vssadmin or wmic commands to delete Volume Shadow Copies — pre-encryption ransomware step.
spl:
index=windows (EventCode=4688 OR EventCode=1)
| where match(CommandLine,
    "(?i)(vssadmin.{0,30}delete|wmic.{0,30}shadowcopy.{0,30}delete|bcdedit.{0,30}recoveryenabled.{0,30}no|wbadmin.{0,30}delete)")
| stats count, values(CommandLine) AS commands, values(Image) AS processes
    BY Computer, User
| eval severity="CRITICAL", mitre_technique="T1490 - Inhibit System Recovery"
| eval action_required="IMMEDIATE ISOLATION — likely active ransomware deployment"
| table Computer, User, commands, processes, severity, mitre_technique, action_required
tuning_notes: Nearly zero legitimate use cases for VSS deletion. Treat as critical and respond immediately.
response: IMMEDIATE: Isolate host from network. Suspend backups to prevent overwrite. Initiate IR procedure. Do NOT reboot.

name: Impossible Travel Detection
description: Detects successful logins from two geographically distinct locations within an implausibly short time window.
log_source: Azure AD / Okta / Auth logs with GeoIP
spl:
index=auth sourcetype=okta action=success
| iplocation src_ip
| stats earliest(_time) AS first_login, latest(_time) AS last_login,
    values(Country) AS countries, values(src_ip) AS ips, count AS logins
    BY user
| eval time_diff_min=round((last_login - first_login)/60, 0)
| where mvcount(countries) > 1 AND time_diff_min < 120
| eval severity="CRITICAL", mitre_technique="T1078 - Valid Accounts (Impossible Travel)"
| eval flag="Login from " + mvjoin(countries," AND ") + " within " + tostring(time_diff_min) + " minutes"
| table user, countries, ips, logins, time_diff_min, flag, severity, mitre_technique
| sort -logins
tuning_notes: VPN users will FP frequently. Integrate with VPN logs to suppress known VPN egress IPs.
response: Suspend account immediately. Notify user via secondary channel. Initiate account takeover investigation.

name: Service Account Anomalous Interactive Login
description: Service accounts should never log in interactively. This detects logon type 2 (interactive) or 10 (remote interactive) for accounts ending in svc_ or _svc.
spl:
index=windows EventCode=4624
    (Logon_Type=2 OR Logon_Type=10)
| where match(Account_Name, "(?i)^svc_|_svc$|service|^sa_")
| where NOT Account_Name="*$"
| stats count, values(Workstation_Name) AS workstations,
    values(Logon_Type) AS logon_types
    BY Account_Name, Source_Network_Address
| eval logon_type_label=mvmap(logon_types,
    case(logon_types=2,"Interactive",logon_types=10,"RemoteInteractive",true(),"Other"))
| eval severity="HIGH", mitre_technique="T1078.002 - Domain Accounts Abuse"
| table Account_Name, Source_Network_Address, count, workstations, logon_type_label, severity, mitre_technique
tuning_notes: Review all service accounts quarterly. Remove interactive logon rights from service accounts via GPO.
response: Investigate source IP. Service account credentials may be compromised. Reset password, review permissions.
